sources.entry: pyinstaller - Converts Python programs into standalone executables (cross-platform).

summary.one_liner: PyInstaller bundles a Python application and all its dependencies into a single folder or executable so it runs without a separately installed Python interpreter.
summary.what_it_does: It analyzes a Python script to discover every module and library the script needs, then collects those files along with the active Python interpreter into one folder or an optional single executable file. It is run from the command line against a main script, for example "pyinstaller /path/to/yourscript.py". The README says it bundles major packages such as numpy, PyQt5/PyQt6, PySide2/PySide6, wxPython and matplotlib out of the box. It also states support for code signing on macOS, bundling of MS Visual C++ DLLs on Windows, and building universal2 apps on macOS. It is installed with pip.
use_cases: package a Python script into a standalone executable
distribute a Python app to users without Python installed
bundle a PyQt or PySide desktop app
build a single-file Windows executable from Python
create a macOS app with code signing
ship a matplotlib or numpy application as one folder
stack: C compiler (gcc or clang) for bootloader build
notable: Not a cross-compiler: build on the target OS
Bundles the Python interpreter together with the app's dependencies
Tested on Windows, macOS and GNU/Linux; used on AIX, Solaris, FreeBSD and OpenBSD
Supports universal2 macOS builds when Python and dependencies are universal2
caveats: Not a cross-compiler; you must run it on each target platform
Python 3.10.0 is unsupported due to a bug, and beta releases of Python 3.16 do not work
Linux needs ldd, objdump and objcopy from system packages; AIX needs a non-static Python library
keywords: make app for users without python
